## Agents and models
- **Custom models for Claude Code:** A Claude Code account can now add its own models from any Anthropic Messages-compatible endpoint, such as LiteLLM, OpenRouter or a Gemini proxy. Give each one a slug, display name, endpoint, API key (kept in the Keychain), custom headers, context window, output limit, auto-compact threshold and reasoning support, and choose which model subagents use. Add, edit and delete them on the Mac or from iPhone and iPad, and pick them in the model picker like any other model. - **Visualizations in the transcript:** When an agent replies with a `<json-render>` block, Controller draws it in place on the Mac and iPhone: cards, tables, lists, bar charts, sparklines, progress bars, metrics, callouts, timelines and more, with a placeholder while the block is still streaming. - **Antigravity subagents stay in their lane:** Tool calls from an Antigravity subagent no longer end or interrupt the parent chat's message or reasoning, and starting a subagent is no longer mistaken for its final reply.
## Terminals and files on your other Macs
- **Terminals look like the Mac's:** A terminal on another Mac now shows its real colors, cursor and font size instead of plain text, on the Mac and on iPhone and iPad. - **A new iPhone terminal:** Type straight into the terminal in a full sheet, switch tabs with larger touch targets, and use a shortcut strip above the keyboard. Scrollback you are reading stays put while new output arrives. - **Documents from another Mac:** PDF, RTF, Office and iWork files in a remote checkout open with Quick Look on the Mac and on iPhone and iPad. - **Text files open again:** Code, Markdown, JSON and plain-text files from another Mac load again. On iPhone, Markdown has the Mac's formatted and source views, links between documents open inside the checkout, and long code lines scroll sideways instead of being cut off.
## Faster and steadier
- Conversations load and save with less work, and the sidebar and pull request list update faster in large workspaces. - Opening sign-in pages and links, reading your Controller account at launch, and starting up no longer pause the interface. - Typing in the iPhone composer no longer searches commands and files on every keystroke.
## Fixed
- Markdown tables that arrived on a single line show as tables again on the Mac and iPhone. - A crash in an agent's command-line tool or a shell is no longer reported as a Controller crash. - A crash on iPhone when background refresh started or ran out of time. - Spurious protocol warnings from Grok and Claude Code housekeeping messages.

## Git and pull requests
- **A new activity card:** The activity card now gathers a chat's workspace in one place: switch between the current checkout, a new worktree or an existing one; open the checkout in Cursor, Zed, Antigravity, VS Code, Xcode or Finder; run project scripts in the Terminal panel; search and switch branches; and commit, push, pull or open a pull request from one button. Its changes row shows the working tree's added and removed lines and opens the diff. - **Generated commit messages and pull requests:** Leave the commit message empty and Controller writes it from the diff, on the Mac and on iPhone and iPad. Choose the account, model and writing style, and how pull request templates are handled, in **Settings → General → Commit & PR Generation**. - **Pull request browser:** The browser has a new look. Under **All**, your own pull requests lead, matched to the account you use on each GitHub host. **Newest** and **Oldest** order pull requests from every project by when they were opened, and dates in comments show in your local time. - **Agents and pull requests:** Agents can search a repository's pull requests, inspect worktrees, and move a chat into an existing worktree or a pull request's checkout.
## Your other Macs
- **Inspector and terminals on another Mac:** Working on a chat from another Mac now opens the inspector with its files and diffs, and terminals run on that Mac. - **Add a project from this Mac first:** The folder card starts on this Mac, and moving between folders is smoother. - **Following a Mac that moved:** A Mac that changes its address is found again even when the directory was being read at the moment it moved.
## Faster and steadier
- Controller does much less work on the main thread: launch, dictation, Keychain access, agent connections, the thread list, transcripts, diffs and pictures all keep the interface responsive while they run. - Pictures in a transcript are decoded once however many places show them, and only a few at a time. - While a reply streams, scrolling up to read no longer pulls you back down, and a reply finishing while the agent keeps working no longer makes the conversation jump.
## Fixed
- A crash when VoiceOver or another accessibility tool read a command approval. - A message continuing after a usage limit, and project details being saved, are kept if you quit at that moment. - An agent connection that could not send a large reply now ends with an error instead of waiting forever. - **⌘F** in the browser reliably puts the cursor in the find field. - The plan chip appears at its full width when you open a chat, and on iPhone it no longer covers the jump-to-latest button, which now works with the keyboard open. - In the narrowest conversation, the model's name shortens instead of pushing the composer past the edge. - On iPhone, the New Chat button is easier to tap.

## Pull requests
- **Work on a pull request:** Attach or check out a GitHub pull request from the sidebar. Open it in a new worktree, in the project folder, or just link it to the chat. Linked pull requests show as badges on their chats, with their state, and the inspector shows their details. - **Agents and pull requests:** Agents can link and unlink pull requests with `link_pull_request` and `unlink_pull_request`, list a chat's pull requests with `list_thread_pull_requests`, and read live details such as the description, mergeability and CI checks with `read_pull_request`. A review can be handed off to another chat.
## Composer
- **@ mentions:** Type **@** in the composer to tag a file in the checkout, another chat, or an open browser tab. `@file:`, `@thread:` and `@tab:` narrow the search. Tags appear as chips you can inspect or remove, show as badges in the sent message, and point the agent at the file path, chat or tab. This works on Mac, iPhone and iPad.
## Usage
- **Antigravity usage:** The Usage window now counts Antigravity's token use. - **Models & Pricing:** Set your own token prices for any model, and link a model's names from different providers into one standardized model so they share a row. Models without a price are listed, with a shortcut to set one.
## iPhone and iPad
- **Larger photos and videos:** Photos and videos up to 100 MB from your Mac's files now preview on iPhone and iPad. Viewed ones are cached on the device until the file changes. - **Diffs:** File diffs use a new viewer, and Antigravity's edits now show diffs per file. - **File links:** Tapping a file citation in a reply opens that file at the cited line.
## Fixed
- File links and citations pointing into worktrees, whose paths contain spaces, now show as links instead of raw Markdown.
